summary: Publishes Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep through Doubleday
entities: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

summary: PKD drafts the Maze/Tench theology notes that develop the colony plot, Delmak setting, divine plurality, the Manufacturer, decay, and the form-destroying principle later associated with A Maze of Death.
source_name: The Maze of Death Theology (Maze notes PDF)
notes: Entered as an early Exegesis-adjacent primary document. The Sarill/multiple-universes/Wheeler lead remains a source-confirmation task.

summary: William Sarill first meets PKD and later spends more than a month as his houseguest during the period associated with the theology behind A Maze of Death.
source_name: William Sarill, Will the Real Ubik Please Stand Up?; A Maze of Death foreword
notes: Sarill confirms the 1968 meeting and extended houseguest period; PKD's Maze foreword credits Sarill as co-developer of the abstract religious system behind the novel.

summary: Hearing "And she shall see the sea" (c. 1968/9).
Writes that he and Roger Zelazny are planning to collaborate on Deus Irae from a 1964 outline Dick had been unable to complete alone.
source_name: Selected Letters Vol. 1, letter to Andy, May 21, 1968

summary: Reads Eastern religious texts including the Bhagavad Gita and Buddhist writings
